headline: Daily market snapshot – August 28 2026
summary: US equity futures mixed with S&P 500 futures -0.12% and Nasdaq-100 futures -0.30%, weighed by Marvell and Rubrik premarket declines. Jackson Hole keynote by Fed Chair Warsh is the main macro event. Oil pulled back on Iran sanctions relief; gold near all-time highs.

headline: Nvidia surges 6% after blowout Q2 FY2027 earnings; Nasdaq lifts nearly 1%
summary: Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 2027 adjusted EPS of $2.22 on revenue of $96.2 billion, beating estimates of $2.09 and $92.2B respectively. Q3 revenue guidance of $105.8B-$110.6B exceeded the $104.8B consensus. Annual revenue doubled year-over-year and the stock jumped 6%, lifting the Nasdaq nearly 1%.
key_facts: Q2 FY27 adj EPS $2.22 vs est $2.09

headline: Marvell Technology sinks 7%+ premarket despite Q2 beat; expectations seen too rich
summary: Marvell Technology reported Q2 revenue of $2.74 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.94, both beating estimates, but shares fell more than 7% in premarket trading on August 28. Analysts noted the stock cannot bounce despite beat as investor expectations remain too rich after the stock's strong run.

headline: Rubrik beats Q2 estimates, raises FY27 outlook; stock falls below $100 in after-hours
summary: Rubrik reported Q2 revenue of $427.26 million and adjusted EPS of $0.22, surpassing estimates of $396.28 million and $0.04. The company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $1.685B-$1.693B and adj EPS to $0.47-$0.53. Despite the beats, shares fell 7.01% in after-hours trading to $99.52.

headline: Salesforce surges 21.6% after crushing Q2 estimates; Agentforce ARR hits $1.5B +240% YoY
summary: Salesforce reported Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $5.90 versus the $3.27 estimate, on revenue of $11.35 billion. The company raised full-year guidance to $46.1B-$46.4B in revenue and Agentforce annual recurring revenue reached $1.5 billion, up 240% year-over-year, confirming AI as a direct revenue driver.

headline: CrowdStrike jumps 19.4% after best-ever quarter; Q2 revenue +26% YoY to $1.47B
summary: CrowdStrike reported fiscal Q2 2027 adjusted EPS of $0.31 on revenue of $1.47 billion, both beating estimates of $0.29 and $1.44B. Revenue grew 26% year-over-year from $1.17B. CEO George Kurtz called it the best quarter in CrowdStrike history, citing AI-driven cybersecurity threats as demand catalyst.
key_facts: CEO: best quarter in company history

headline: CrowdStrike lifts annual revenue forecast on surging AI cybersecurity demand
summary: CrowdStrike raised its annual revenue forecast after Q2 results beat expectations. The company cited rising AI-driven cybersecurity threats as the primary demand driver, positioning the security platform as a direct beneficiary of artificial intelligence proliferation in enterprise environments.

headline: Fed Chair Warsh delivers inaugural Jackson Hole keynote at 10am ET; signals focus on long-term issues
summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivered his first Jackson Hole keynote speech on August 28 at 10am ET, choosing to frame long-term structural economic questions rather than signal near-term rate moves. Warsh has noted the Fed is 'not constrained by market prices.' Three regional Fed presidents previously dissented in favor of rate hikes at the July meeting.
key_facts: First Warsh Jackson Hole keynote 10am ET Aug 28
Focus on long-term structural questions, not near-term guidance
Warsh: Fed 'not constrained by market prices'
Three regional presidents dissented for hikes at July meeting

headline: July 2026 PCE inflation stays at 3.7% YoY, above forecast; core unchanged at 3.3%
summary: The July PCE price index rose 3.7% year-over-year, exceeding the 3.6% estimate, and 0.2% month-over-month versus the 0.1% forecast. Core PCE held at 3.3% annually and 0.2% monthly. The sticky reading reinforced a higher-for-longer Fed stance and pushed September rate hike odds above 40%.
key_facts: Sep rate hike probability raised to ~40%

headline: CME FedWatch: 40% probability of September FOMC rate hike after hot PCE
summary: CME Group FedWatch shows fed funds futures pricing approximately 40% probability of a 25 basis point rate increase at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting, up from 33% the prior week following the above-consensus July PCE. The current benchmark rate stands at 3.50-3.75% and nine of 18 FOMC members have penciled in at least one 2026 hike.
key_facts: CME FedWatch 40% probability of Sep rate hike
9 of 18 FOMC members penciled in at least one 2026 hike

headline: UMich August consumer sentiment falls to 51, missing 54.5 estimate; ends two-month recovery
summary: The University of Michigan's final August consumer sentiment index fell to 51 from 55.2 in July, missing the 54.5 estimate and ending two consecutive months of improvement. The current conditions index fell to 51.8 and the expectations measure to 50.6. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.3%.
key_facts: UMich Aug sentiment 51 vs est 54.5, prior 55.2

headline: US-Canada trade war escalates: 50% tariffs on $20B Canadian goods now in effect
summary: US 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion of Canadian goods covering 500+ product categories took effect August 22 after trade talks failed. Impacted categories include dairy, alcohol, electronics, building materials, and apparel. Canada announced counter-tariffs on 700+ US items including steel, dairy, and electronics effective September 8.
key_facts: US 50% tariffs on ~$20B Canadian goods effective Aug 22
Canada counter-tariffs on 700+ US items effective Sept 8
PM Carney: Canada is 'at war' with US

headline: Canada to impose counter-tariffs on US steel, dairy, electronics starting September 8
summary: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs covering more than 700 US product categories effective September 8, 2026, targeting US steel, dairy, and electronics industries in response to the 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods that took effect August 22. Prime Minister Carney described the measures as Canada defending its national interests in an economic war with the US.
key_facts: Canada counter-tariffs on 700+ US items effective Sept 8
Response to US 50% tariffs effective Aug 22
PM Carney: Canada 'at war' with US

headline: Bank of Korea raises rate to 3% in back-to-back hike; upgrades GDP forecast to 3.3%
summary: The Bank of Korea raised its seven-day repurchase rate by 25 basis points to 3% in a 6-1 decision on August 27, its second consecutive increase. Governor Shin called it a preemptive action as July CPI at 2.8% exceeds the 2% target. The 2026 GDP growth forecast was raised to 3.3% from 2.6%, driven by semiconductor exports.

headline: US weighs new sweeping tariffs on foreign semiconductors in laptops, servers, gaming hardware
summary: The Trump administration is considering a second round of tariffs targeting foreign semiconductors embedded in consumer and enterprise devices including laptops, data center servers, and gaming consoles. A duty-free quota tied to pledged US production is under consideration. A first round of 25% chip tariffs took effect January 15, 2026.
key_facts: US mulling tariffs on foreign chips in laptops, servers, gaming consoles
Duty-free quota pegged to US production pledges under consideration
Plan in early stage, staggered rollout reportedly under consideration
Would affect data centers and consumer electronics

headline: Asia markets mixed Aug 28: Nikkei +0.81%, KOSPI -1% on chip drag, Hang Seng recovers
summary: Asian markets showed mixed performance on August 28. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.81% to 66,665, led by IT services stocks NEC and Fujitsu near +4%. South Korea's KOSPI fell approximately 1% as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix remained under pressure. The Hang Seng erased an early 0.3% loss, and Shanghai fell 0.11% to 3,952.
key_facts: BOK second rate hike weighed on Seoul

headline: KOSPI falls ~1% as Samsung, SK Hynix remain under pressure; US chip tariff risk adds headwind
summary: South Korea's KOSPI fell approximately 1% on August 28, with memory chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix continuing to slide. The Bank of Korea's second consecutive rate increase to 3% and reported US consideration of broad semiconductor tariffs compounded pressure on Korean chip exporters.
key_facts: Samsung and SK Hynix remain lower
BOK raised rate to 3%, second consecutive hike
US semiconductor tariff consideration weighs on supply chain

headline: European markets open: FTSE 100 flat at 10,792, DAX +0.44% on NVDA AI lift
summary: European equities opened mixed on August 28, with the FTSE 100 unchanged at 10,792 and the German DAX gaining 0.44%. The broader Stoxx 600 has rallied 11% year-to-date, with regional benchmarks near record highs. August 2026 has been unusually strong versus historical seasonal weakness.

headline: Victory Capital to acquire First Eagle Investments for $7B, creating $571B AUM manager
summary: Victory Capital Holdings agreed to acquire First Eagle Investments from Genstar Capital for approximately $7 billion, comprising $4 billion cash and $2 billion in new shares plus $575 million in assumed debt. The transaction creates a $571 billion AUM diversified global asset manager and continues consolidation in the fee-pressured asset management industry.
key_facts: First Eagle AUM $222B as of July 31

headline: Murdoch family considering re-merging Fox Corp and News Corp; shares volatile on Reuters report
summary: Reuters reported that Rupert and Lachlan Murdoch are contemplating recombining Fox Corp and News Corp, based on unsealed court documents and testimony from a family succession case. Shares of both companies showed volatile trading with volume spikes. A 2022 attempt to merge the companies failed after investors pushed back.

Both stocks volatile with elevated volume
Previous 2022 merger attempt failed on investor opposition

Dow futures edged up 0.07% and Russell 2000 futures rose 0.04%. Markets await Chicago PMI and UMich final sentiment alongside Warsh's 10am Jackson Hole speech.
key_facts: Warsh Jackson Hole speech at 10am ET

headline: Oil slips Aug 28: WTI $82.92 -0.73%, Brent $88.22 -0.34%; gold $4,629 near all-time high
summary: Oil prices slipped on August 28 as US sanctions on Iran proved less aggressive than markets initially feared. WTI crude fell 0.73% to $82.92 and Brent declined 0.34% to $88.22. Gold pulled back 0.75% to $4,629.06 but remains near all-time highs. Brent is up 30.73% year-over-year.
key_facts: Iran sanctions less aggressive than feared weighing on oil

headline: Gold near all-time highs at $4,629 as geopolitical risk, sticky inflation support demand
summary: Gold remains near its all-time highs of approximately $4,647-$4,650 set earlier in August, trading at $4,629 on August 28 despite a 0.75% pullback. Elevated inflation at 3.7% PCE, geopolitical tensions from US-Iran sanctions and the US-Canada trade war, and a higher-for-longer Fed environment have driven gold's sustained advance.
key_facts: US-Iran sanctions and US-Canada tariffs supporting safe-haven demand
Warsh Jackson Hole speech potential catalyst

headline: Bitcoin holds ~$79K pulling back from $81K high; Ethereum near $2,499
summary: Bitcoin was trading around $78,500-$79,000 on August 28, pulling back from its August 25 high of $81,023.41 but maintaining broad strength. The weekly gain through August 24 was approximately 22%. Ethereum was near $2,499. Crypto prices have been supported by Digital Assets Clarity Act legislative momentum.
key_facts: Digital Assets Clarity Act momentum supporting crypto

headline: 10-year Treasury at 4.65-4.68% ahead of Warsh speech; PCE supports higher-for-longer
summary: US Treasury yields were steady on August 28, with the 10-year note at 4.65-4.68% and the 2-year at 4.24%. The 30-year yield stands at 5.20%. Above-consensus July PCE data at 3.7% YoY supports the market's higher-for-longer rate pricing. Markets await Warsh's Jackson Hole speech for any policy signals.
key_facts: Warsh Jackson Hole speech at 10am ET

headline: EUR/USD steady at 1.1658; USD/JPY 159.38 as BOJ September hike priced at 87%
summary: The euro traded at 1.1658 against the US dollar on August 28. The yen was slightly weaker, with USD/JPY at 159.38, as markets price an 87% probability of a Bank of Japan rate hike to 1.25% in September, sharply up from 23% before the BOJ's July meeting. The yen has ranged 158.53-159.48 in the past week.

headline: AI earnings trifecta: NVDA, CRM, CRWD all beat, confirming AI as direct revenue driver
summary: A rare alignment of AI-sector earnings saw Nvidia, Salesforce, and CrowdStrike all beat estimates and raise guidance, confirming that artificial intelligence is driving measurable revenue across chips and software. Market observers noted that software and chips were 'on the same page for once.' Salesforce's Agentforce ARR at $1.5B and CrowdStrike citing AI threats as a demand driver were the headline AI signals.

CrowdStrike: AI cybersecurity threats driving demand
Software and chips showing concurrent AI revenue growth
